_say: "say" is what the voice is sent (phonetic spellings of Finnish names); "text" is the caption. Same number of words in both.

lines.text: You lead cancer care in Lapland.
Of a hundred of your lung cancer patients, eighteen are treated to cure.
Lapland's patients do not wait longer: thirty-one days from diagnosis to treatment, thirty-seven in Finland.
Fewer are treated to cure. About twelve patients a year.
Is the gap real? Not chance, not age, not just missing records.
Stage at diagnosis is not published: an eight-week records audit settles it.
Six actions, for two hundred and eleven thousand five hundred euros a year.
By the model, five of those twelve patients are treated to cure. Forty-three percent of the gap.
Precise radiotherapy, for early cancer that cannot be operated: thirty thousand four hundred euros a year. First step: write the referral rule. Owner: the chief of oncology.
But is it already running? Kello checks the web, live, through Oxylabs.
It searches, reads the hospital's own pages, and quotes them.
This morning's check and the live run agree: Oulu University Hospital already offers it. Ask them first.
That goes straight into the plan: one page, in English or Finnish, ready to send.
Every number opens its source: Gemini read nine hundred and sixty-six registry values, each with its page and quote.
We ask for a six-month pilot of two actions: a chest surgeon reviews every decision not to operate, and those who cannot be operated get radiotherapy.
The goal: from eighteen and a half to twenty and a half percent treated to cure, by 2028.
